usage: claude-pace [-h] [--watch] [--alerts-only] [--json] [--target TARGET]
                   [--band BAND] [--interval INTERVAL] [--plan {fill,even}]
                   [--reserve RESERVE] [--redeem-margin HOURS] [--state STATE]
                   [--notify CMD]

Pace agent work against Claude Code and Codex usage windows, including banked
resets, and say how many more agent lanes the headroom supports. `plan` reads
both once and recommends where spare work should go. It never redeems a reset.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --watch
  --alerts-only
  --json
  --target TARGET
  --band BAND
  --interval INTERVAL
  --plan {fill,even}
  --reserve RESERVE     with --plan fill, pace like --plan even once the long
                        window has this many points left
  --redeem-margin HOURS
                        aim to fill a window to 100% this many hours before a
                        banked reset expires; at the limit, keep a banked
                        reset (nothing expires first) if the window resets on
                        its own within this many hours
  --state STATE
  --notify CMD          run CMD with the alert text as its last argument on
                        each alert or reset

Lane headroom: per-lane burn is a window's recent burn over the lanes active
meanwhile, time-weighted (each count covers the 10 minutes before it). Usage
comes in whole points, so a rate needs to be known to within a third: two
steps up timed by the readings around them, use moving 3 points, or a stretch
of a fifth of the window, which bounds the burn by one point more than it
moved. Until then it says "measuring"; a short window's status uses the same
rate. A window that cannot be measured does not hold the source at "measuring"
if, after its first hour, even twice its average burn would end it at or below
its aim.
